name: FFmpeg
summary: A media-processing framework organized around format contexts, packet/frame codec APIs, and linked filter graphs that transform streams between input and output representations.

features.name: Format-context stream boundary
features.description: libavformat uses AVFormatContext as the main context for muxing and demuxing. The fixed header describes an input or output format, an I/O context, and an array of AVStreams; demuxing creates streams while muxing creates them before writing the header, then packets are read or written through the context.
benefits: Separates container I/O and stream metadata from codec processing
Provides explicit input and output lifecycle operations
costs: Container behavior and timing must be coordinated across packets
Input discovery and output setup have different ownership rules
Format-specific options widen the integration surface

features.name: Decoupled codec send/receive pipeline
features.description: libavcodec exposes separate send and receive functions for decoding and encoding. The fixed header documents input submission, output polling, internal buffering, draining with NULL input, and a strict state-machine constraint preventing simultaneous EAGAIN from both sides.
benefits: Decouples input submission from output production
Uses one API shape for audio/video encoding and decoding
costs: Callers must implement polling, draining, and EAGAIN handling
Buffering adds latency and memory considerations
The API is stateful and misuse can stall progress

features.name: Linked filter graph with negotiated media formats
features.description: libavfilter represents filters with input and output pads connected by AVFilterLink objects. The fixed header records source and destination contexts, media type, and current audio/video fields on links, and documents format lists used to negotiate the format actually used.
benefits: Composes media transformations as graph nodes
Supports explicit pad and link topology
Makes media-type and format compatibility part of graph construction
costs: Graph construction must satisfy pad and format constraints
Negotiation can require conversion or reject a topology
Dynamic and hardware-frame contexts increase lifecycle complexity

features.name: Codec initialization parameter validation
features.description: The fixed revision's Nellymoser decoder rejects a non-positive sample rate during initialization before allocating and configuring decoder state. This is a local example of validating caller-supplied codec parameters at a codec boundary.
benefits: Rejects invalid state before decode processing
Makes codec preconditions visible at initialization
Prevents processing from relying on an invalid sample-rate assumption
costs: Boundary validation adds a failure mode to setup

mathematical_views.question: How do container streams, codec packet/frame transformations, filters, and output streams compose into a media workflow?
assumptions: Nodes expose media-type-specific inputs and outputs
Edges carry packets, frames, or negotiated stream data
Codec algorithms and bitstream details are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which input and output operations are valid while a codec buffers, drains, or reports lack of progress?
assumptions: Input and output operations are separate
EAGAIN and EOF are state-dependent outcomes

mathematical_views.question: Can a proposed filter topology be linked while satisfying media type and format constraints at every edge?
assumptions: Each edge has one source and destination pad
Endpoint format lists define negotiation candidates
Hardware-frame context is an additional edge property

costs: Demux/mux lifecycle and timestamp interleaving add state

benefits: Supports buffered codecs with a uniform polling interface
costs: Callers must reason about backpressure and draining
Negotiation and pad compatibility constrain graphs

benefits: Fails early at a codec precondition boundary
